Modified read using the May 2017 Beige Book: The FOMC’s June statement is moderately positive—acknowledging continued labor market strengthening, firming household spending, and ongoing business investment—while remaining cautious as inflation runs below 2% and the Committee proceeds with gradual tightening and plans for balance sheet normalization. The May Beige Book corroborates a modest-to-moderate pace of growth across most Districts, with broadly tightening labor markets and wage pressures concentrated in skilled occupations. It also flags mixed consumer conditions (particularly softer autos), housing strength alongside more cautious commercial real estate (especially retail), lending volumes that mirror the general economy rather than surge, and improving energy-sector activity and tourism. These Beige Book nuances—credit conditions not uniformly accommodative (notably tighter in autos, cautious in CRE), modest overall wage and price pressures, and uneven sectoral momentum—temper the upbeat elements and reinforce a guarded, data-dependent stance consistent with the Kashkari dissent. Net: still positive, but slightly less upbeat than a plain read of the statement.
